item.title: Iranian FM arrives in Ashgabat for official visit to Turkmenistan

item.title: Iranian FM congratulates Algeria on National Day
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi, in a message to Algerian Foreign Minister Ahmed Attaf, congratulated the Algerian nation and government on the 72nd anniversary of the launch of the liberation revolution and Algeria’s National Day. In his message, the Iranian foreign minister wished prosperity and well-being for the government and great people of Algeria and expressed hope that Iran and Algeria, by continuing their active and constructive approach in supporting justice-oriented causes, would see their joint efforts strengthened and make greater use of their existing capacities to further expand cooperation at the bilateral, regional, and international levels.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, while condemning the anti-Iranian policies and actions of the British government, which are contrary to the principles of the United Nations Charter and international law, particularly the principle of respect for national sovereignty and the prohibition of resorting to unlawful measures against other countries, reaffirms the determination of the Government of the Islamic Republic of Iran to take the necessary measures to safeguard Iran’s national security and interests. Accordingly, and pursuant to a resolution of the country’s Supreme National Security Council, in response to the British government’s hostile actions against the Islamic Republic of Iran over the past year, including its involvement in the US-Israeli imposed war against Iran through the provision of military and logistical bases and facilities located in territories under British jurisdiction, as well as that government’s decision on July 13, 2026 to place the Islamic Revolution Guard Corps (IRGC) under the State Threats Act 2026, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs announces the following: A) As of the issuance of this statement (November 1, 2026), the UK’s Secret Intelligence Service (MI6) shall be classified as a “hostile group” pursuant to Note 2 to Article 1 of the Law on “Enhancing Punishments for Espionage and Cooperation with the Zionist Regime and Hostile Countries Against National Security and Interests,” and the provisions of this law shall apply to the British agency B) As of the issuance of this statement (November 1, 2026), the UK’s Royal Navy and Royal Air Force shall be subject to the Law on “Countermeasures Against the United States’ Designation of the Islamic Revolution Guard Corps as a Terrorist Organization” and shall accordingly be designated as terrorist organizations. It is self-evident that these measures have been adopted in accordance with the principles of international law and within the framework of the principle of reciprocity, and the British government shall bear responsibility for their consequences.

item.title: Baqaei: Blaming Iran for US crimes attempt to whitewash aggression
item.description: Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei, reacting to claims by the so-called Iran Human Rights Reporting Mechanism, wrote on X that using the mechanism to blame Iran for crimes committed by the United States and Israel was a deliberate attempt to whitewash aggression and crimes. "Regardless of the politically motivated nature of the mandate imposed on the Human Rights Council by the UK، exploiting the so-called Special Rapporteurship on the Situation of Human Rights in Iran to blame Iran for the crimes committed by the US and Israel amounts to nothing less than a deliberate attempt to whitewash aggression, atrocities, and unilateral coercive measures. Such an approach is deeply misleading and profoundly disingenous."

item.title: Baqaei strongly condemns UAE-Canada interference over Iranian islands
item.description: Esmail Baqaei, Spokesperson for Iran’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, strongly condemned the brazen and interventionist claims made by the United Arab Emirates and Canada regarding Iran’s three islands, as stated in a joint statement by the Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi and the Canadian Prime Minister. He stressed that Abu Musa, Greater Tunb and Lesser Tunb are an inseparable and eternal part of Iran’s territory, adding that the repetition of baseless and unfounded claims about these islands would not change the established geographical, historical and legal realities. Condemning Canada’s deplorable move to align itself with the UAE government in making territorial claims against Iran, the Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson noted that such an action by Canada—which itself faces territorial claims by the US ruling establishment—is short-sighted, violates the fundamental principles of the United Nations Charter, and runs counter to international law, entailing the international responsibility of the Canadian government. Baqaei advised the UAE government to abide by the principle of good neighborliness instead of repeatedly making futile territorial claims against a major neighboring country.

item.title: Iran’s new ambassador to Greece meets with FM Araghchi
item.description: Mahmoud Heidari, the new ambassador of the Islamic Republic of Iran to Greece, met with Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi before departing for his diplomatic mission. During the meeting, the new ambassador outlined his proposed plan for Tehran–Athens relations and for utilizing existing capacities to expand cooperation in various fields. The foreign minister wished the new ambassador success in his mission and, referring to the historical background of relations between Iran and Greece as two ancient civilizations, stressed the need to pursue and strengthen relations between the Islamic Republic of Iran and Greece within the framework of agreements and cooperation documents between the two countries. Before being appointed as Iran’s ambassador to Greece, Mahmoud Heidari served as an assistant to the foreign minister and director general for Mediterranean and Eastern European affairs at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

item.title: Iran FM: Sustainable regional security requires collective responsibility
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi wrote in an Instagram post that the recent four-way meeting in Tehran with defense and security officials from Iran, Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan provided a valuable opportunity to advance dialogue on regional peace and security and jointly address threats and challenges, stressing that sustainable security must be ensured through regional countries’ participation without military presence or intervention by extra-regional powers.

item.title: Iranian Jordanian FMs hold phone talks discuss regional developments
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi and Jordanian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi held a phone conversation on Tuesday morning to discuss regional developments. During the conversation, Araghchi outlined Iran’s positions on regional developments and stressed the need for Islamic countries and the international community to take serious action to counter the continued genocide and expansionism of the occupying Zionist regime. Recalling the devastating consequences of the US and Israeli military aggression against Iran for the region and the world, the Iranian foreign minister emphasized that restoring security to the region requires an end to the United States’ aggressive and interventionist actions, as well as containing the Zionist regime’s expansionism and warmongering. Araghchi also condemned the terrorist attack on a church in southern Jordan and expressed his condolences to the families of those killed in the incident. The foreign ministers of the two countries underscored the importance of making use of diplomacy and continuing political consultations to safeguard peace and stability in the region.
